Investment Snapshot

Zoned, Level & Serviced

Most land plays start with an entitlement fight. This one doesn't. The I-2 designation is already on the parcel, so the first question is which compatible use pencils best — not whether the city will allow industrial at all. Financing Fit

Land and industrial deals don't fit a one-size lender box. Through our lending partners we can discuss creative deal structure on this site.

  • Commercial land financing
  • Industrial acquisition loan
  • Private money
  • Seller financing (subject to seller terms)
  • Owner-user financing
  • Development financing
  • Stabilization → commercial refinance
Refinance and DSCR-style underwriting apply only once the yard is improved, leased, and producing stabilized NOI — not to the land in its current vacant state.

Multi-Tenant Upside

Instead of one bulk lease, the site can be split into separately fenced contractor compounds. Smaller yards diversify tenant risk and may lift total revenue — local rents need to be tested before underwriting it.

  • Roofing
  • Excavation
  • Concrete
  • Landscaping
  • Plumbing / HVAC
  • Utility contractors
  • Equipment operators
  • Restoration
  • General construction
  • Fleet operators
  • Material suppliers
  • Logistics users

Actual rents vary with surfacing, fencing, access, security, net usable acreage, and whether the site leases as one yard or several. Gross figures before operating expenses, insurance, and taxes.

Due Diligence Checklist

Gross acres and leasable acres are not the same number. The pond, drainage, setbacks, and access will drive both income and development capacity.

  • Confirm I-2 permitted uses, IOS / outdoor-storage approval, and self-storage requirements if pursued
  • Phase I Environmental and boundary survey
  • Wetlands, floodplain / floodway, pond and drainage evaluation
  • Soil / geotechnical testing for any construction
  • Utility and sewer connection location & capacity
  • Stormwater engineering
  • Ingress / egress, truck turning radius, curb-cut requirements
  • Fencing / screening requirements and setbacks
Value-Add Strategy

Four-Phase Exit Path

A value-add real estate play that can start producing income without vertical construction, then scale as the market supports it.

01

IOS / Laydown Yard

Fence, secure, and improve usable acreage. Lease to contractor, fleet, equipment, or material-storage users.

02

Multi-Tenant IOS

Carve separately secured compounds to diversify tenants and push total revenue.

03

Industrial Flex

Add warehouse / flex space while keeping outdoor yard area — a format already proven in Anderson.

04

Full Development

Warehouse / distribution, contractor facilities, owner-user, or manufacturing support.

Acquire→Improve Phase 1→Lease Yard→Establish NOI→Refinance / Expand
